- No exclusion headers like "Mahnung" or "Zahlungserinnerung" → proceed.

2. Header validation and anchors
- Invoice date anchor: "Datum: 22.11.2023".
- Grand total / Endbetrag anchor: "Endbetrag ... EUR 14.275,80".
- VAT group line: "Umsatzsteuer 10,000 % ... 1.297,80" with base line "12.978,00".
- Sender VAT/UID anchor: "UID-Nr.: ATU39247604" in footer.

3. Field mapping and numeric parsing decisions
- GrandTotal.Amount candidate: "14.275,80" (Austrian format: dot as thousands sep, comma as decimal) → numeric value 14275.80.
- Invoice.Date: "22.11.2023" (use as string).
- Sender.VatId: "ATU39247604" (exact as shown).
- Vat.Rate: text shows "10,000 %" — interpreted as 10.000% → numeric value 10 (per rule: remove %; keep decimals as in input — original shows three decimals "10,000" which would correspond to 10.000; schema expects number; will represent as 10 or 10.000 depending on final numeric formatting).
- Net.Amount: "12.978,00" → numeric 12978.00.
- Vat.Amount: "1.297,80" → numeric 1297.80.

4. No-inference and formatting rules applied
- No other VAT groups present; all amounts extracted correspond to the invoice-wide VAT group.
- Preserve decimal precision consistent with input (two decimals for amounts). Do not invent missing values.
- If multiple formats ambiguous (e.g., Vat.Rate "10,000"), plan to represent as numeric 10.0 or 10.000 preserving original decimal precision.

5. Conclusion
- Document qualifies as invoice. Extractable values identified: Invoice.Date = "22.11.2023"; Sender.VatId = "ATU39247604"; GrandTotal.Amount = 14275.80; Net.Amount = 12978.00; Vat.Amount = 1297.80; Vat.Rate = 10 (with original three-decimal form 10.000 noted).
